question: Matthew's hypothesis: M extends the game for social stories, about the whole system; N extends it for stress tests, of the whole system. Does the record of their requests bear that out?
tickets: three castles, each child's own (N's, M's, and one for D), with rooms
the castle designer and its seven room kinds
castle colours: banners in two colours, the owner's letter always readable (M's gold letter on a gold banner did not show)
a contrast rule for the letter
no skeletons unless asked for: the dungeons were too scary for M
a slider per dungeon, starting at 0; a design rule (nothing scary unless asked for)
a drawing fault M caught (the lantern), then a pass over all such faults
a sweep of lines past their shapes
a hallway whose stairs lead nowhere ends in a wall
a wall drawn where the stairs were
a dining room: a long table, 4 to 18 places at it, torches, candles, chandeliers
a new room kind, drawn in perspective
eight ways out of the hallway and the dining room
side doors to 3 a side, far and near walls
doors closer, signs bigger, the screen used to the full
ears, in every view: three shapes and a size
ears facing us and in profile, under hair and hoods
an on-screen controller: the iPad has no USB port for the game controller
a pad drawn on the screen, as a real pad to the game
in World design, ways off the map can't be turned on; a way that would fix a warning is starred
a dark theme over the whole game
an "all passageways" button in World design
joining every pair of neighbouring squares that both have the way
what's new, in the game: every version's notes, so M can read the recent features as we work
a grass hut: outside, and a living room, a bedroom and a potion room inside
the grass hut round, inside and out
round rooms: a wall curving round a flat floor
a cluster of grass huts, one to six rooms, with a hut center
huts in pairs, triads and rings
more couch-cushion raves, and more turtle steppers dubs, upbeat
a pop-up when a new version is out
a version check, off unless switched on
a lever wired to a trap door does not open it
a wiring bug: levers and trap doors now join in either order
lichen, to decorate rocks, castle walls and logs
the trap room's levers do nothing to a touch on M's iPad
a touch event dropped between pointerdown and touchstart
new places behind the camp, the falls and the clearing: inside every tent, the cave behind the waterfall
tents and a cave, each a place with its own way in and out
where feet can stand in each place (rivers, the pool, the campfire)
the first ground shapes: the start of the collision system
a visibility panel: each body part see-through, invisible, or a ghost
our imagination too slow to walk in on the black laptop (N's old laptop)
falling into the castle's pits, landing in the dungeon below
a fall and a landing, pits as holes
N put as many cauldrons as he could in a place, and the black laptop ground to a halt
a frame-rate watch per thing, red boxes on the costliest
N ignored the red boxes and kept adding cauldrons until it froze again
a latch: nothing more added while a red box stands
a trap room's pit shapes belong to that room (a bug in N's room 3)
bubbles: a place group, and a room made of bubble foam
boulder levers: boulders fall from the ceiling onto the pits
boulders, then their speeds (ticket 328) and fallen rocks to move (ticket 338)
hit by a falling boulder, the friend bursts into rainbow bubbles and comes back
pull the levers without walking to them, to stand where the boulder falls
an Advanced toggle restoring the old pull

kinds.story: a story, a home, or something of one's own
kinds.edge: rules pushed to their edges: falling, boulders, being hit
kinds.stress: load: as many as possible, until it breaks

mentions them (a night's work while they gave no suggestions)
a page about the game and them
